actions.justification: Mandatory first step in transfusion evaluation - assess hemodynamic stability to determine urgency of transfusion need.
Mandatory assessment to determine if patient has ongoing blood loss, which affects transfusion strategy and thresholds.
Mandatory lab to establish baseline hemoglobin, hematocrit, platelets, and guide transfusion threshold decisions.

Mandatory action required within 60 minutes. Type and screen is essential for transfusion preparedness to identify blood type and detect alloantibodies before any potential blood product administration.
Mandatory action required within 60 minutes. Reviewing prior transfusion history is critical to identify previous transfusion reactions, alloantibodies, and inform safe blood product selection.

Assessing symptoms of anemia (fatigue, dyspnea, angina, dizziness) is needed to determine whether a liberal (Hb >8) or restrictive transfusion threshold applies and guide decision-making after CBC results are reviewed.

Patient is hemodynamically stable (HR 80, BP 120/80, SpO2 98%) with no signs of active bleeding or hemodynamic compromise. Evidence-based guidelines support a restrictive transfusion threshold (Hb <7-8 g/dL) in stable patients to minimize transfusion-related risks.
Pre-medication with acetaminophen is recommended prior to blood transfusion to reduce the risk of febrile non-hemolytic transfusion reactions, a common transfusion complication.
Pre-medication with diphenhydramine (antihistamine) is indicated prior to transfusion to reduce the risk of allergic transfusion reactions, particularly in patients with transfusion history.
Ensure reliable IV access is maintained while awaiting CBC results and in case transfusion or other IV medications are needed based on lab results.
Maintain normothermia to prevent coagulopathy and adverse outcomes, particularly important in patients who may require transfusion.
Patient is stable but requires serial vital sign monitoring every 15 minutes to detect any hemodynamic changes while awaiting CBC results and to ensure ongoing stability.
Coagulation status monitoring is important in the transfusion context to assess for any coagulopathy and guide further transfusion decisions once CBC returns.
Tranexamic acid may be indicated if there is evidence or concern for active bleeding or ongoing blood loss in a transfusion patient, to reduce fibrinolysis and support hemostasis.
Order Direct Antiglobulin Test (DAT) to evaluate for hemolytic transfusion reaction, which is an important safety consideration in this transfusion patient.
Reticulocyte count helps characterize the anemia etiology (hypoproliferative vs. hemolytic/blood loss) and guides further management decisions.
Iron studies will help determine if iron deficiency is contributing to the anemia, which would influence long-term management strategy.

Patient vitals are currently stable (HR 80, BP 120/80, SpO2 98%), but labs including CBC are still pending at 85 minutes. Serial hemodynamic reassessment is indicated to detect any deterioration while awaiting results.
CBC is still pending; reassessing hemoglobin trend is critical to guide transfusion decisions and determine if thresholds for intervention have been met.

Thromboelastography (TEG) provides real-time assessment of coagulation status and can guide targeted hemostatic therapy, particularly relevant given the transfusion context and monitoring of coagulation already underway.
Blood bank workup including type and crossmatch is essential to prepare compatible blood products if transfusion becomes necessary. Labs are still pending and this ensures readiness.
Apply restrictive transfusion threshold strategy - transfuse if hemoglobin falls below 8 g/dL once CBC results return, consistent with evidence-based transfusion guidelines for stable patients.
If transfusion is anticipated or ongoing, calcium gluconate should be available to counteract hypocalcemia from citrate in blood products, particularly relevant if multiple units are administered.

CBC is still pending; pre-authorizing transfusion of pRBC if hemoglobin returns below 7 g/dL is appropriate given the restrictive transfusion strategy already in place for this hemodynamically stable patient.
